implementation_notes: ActiveRecord's default metadata source is not the model file but the database: when the class is first used the connection reads the table's columns and the framework defines typed attribute methods from that introspection, with ModelSchema's table_name/primary_key/column_names and the Attribute API (attribute :name, :string, default: ...) as the explicit override layer. The engine is ActiveRecord::Base itself - CRUD, dirty tracking and query building all read the introspected metadata - so there is no per-model mapper to write. Use an explicit dataset or repository when you want the mapping declared rather than inferred, since introspection ties model loading to a live connection.
code_sketch:
class User < ApplicationRecord
  self.table_name = "users"
  attribute :name, :string, default: ""
  validates :name, presence: true
end
pitfalls: Introspection means the class needs a live connection to load: models cannot be used without the database, which couples bootstrapping order to schema availability.
Schema drift surfaces as runtime NoMethodError or silently missing attributes, since the mapping is read at boot rather than compiled.
Database defaults and attribute-API defaults are separate layers that disagree easily, giving values that differ depending on whether the record was loaded or built.

variants.name: Sequel models over an explicit dataset
variants.implementation_notes: Sequel separates the mapping into an explicit dataset: Sequel::Model(:users) or set_dataset selects the relation, the model's column metadata comes from that dataset's schema (Model.columns and db_schema, which can be declared with set_schema or introspected), and plugins add the remaining behaviour such as validation helpers or optimistic locking. The engine is Sequel's dataset query builder, and because the dataset is an ordinary object, models can be built over views, subqueries or a different database in the same process - flexibility ActiveRecord's convention-driven mapping does not offer.
variants.code_sketch:
class User < Sequel::Model(:users)
  plugin :validation_helpers
  def validate
    validates_presence [:name]
  end
end
pitfalls: Column metadata still comes from the database by default, so the same loading and drift caveats apply; explicitly declared schemas must be kept in step with the table by hand.
The dataset is mutable state: reassigning Model.dataset changes the mapping for every instance and is a classic source of 'wrong table' bugs.
